concept: KanbanBoard is a rack of named columns on one panel with a card in each slot, like the cards on a production rack: a card changes column by a hand, by a named key or by the arrow keys, and the count of each column is read from its own small window. Dragging is one way to move a card and never the only way.

default_to_avoid.pattern: kanban board whose cards move only by dragging between pastel columns with coloured count badges
default_to_avoid.why_not: A drag-only board cannot be reached from a keyboard or a screen reader, and coloured badges tell the limit by hue alone, which breaks P2 and the rule that status is never told by colour.

default_to_avoid.pattern: task board as grey rounded columns with white cards, a drop shadow from straight above and a blue add button in every column
default_to_avoid.why_not: Boxes inside boxes with one drop shadow and a blue key per column spend the single orange and the single light of the unit on decoration.

references.source: Toyota kanban card rack (Taiichi Ohno, 1950s): named bays on a board, one card per job, moved by a hand from bay to bay and counted against a limit
Vitsoe 606 Universal Shelving System (Dieter Rams, 1960): fixed tracks with items slotted at set positions and moved by hand without tools
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: listbox pattern, rearrangeable options (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/listbox/examples/listbox-rearrangeable/)
Card in this system: each task is a Card with its lit lip, imported and not redrawn; the Move key is the Menu of this system

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: Each column prints how many cards it holds in a small window cut into the body, with the limit beside the count when there is one, and a column with no cards shows a recessed slot.

derivation.consequence: the display is a live region (polite) and never a control
derivation.form: A polite status says which card moved, to which column and to what position, and the count windows are printing that takes no focus.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: A card takes Alt with the arrow keys to change column or position, the arrows alone walk the cards of a column, and the Move key opens a choice of columns, so no move needs a pointer.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The grip and the Move key are 44px targets set in the card's header, and the dots they print are smaller than the target that holds them.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: Each column title stands on the inset line of its column, level with its count window, and the card titles start on the inset line of the card.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: Columns keep their width and their place when cards arrive or leave, and the drop mark is a line drawn on a card's edge, so nothing shifts while a card is being carried.

derivation.consequence: shadows are short and soft; a unit never floats more than its material height
derivation.form: A card being carried rises by the shadow of a pressed key at most, and returns to the plain card height the moment it is dropped.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: Nothing on the board is orange; a limit that is passed is told by a warning mark and the figures, so the one orange stays with the key that saves the board.

options.name: columns as recessed wells holding raised cards
open columns split by a seam, with the count in a small recessed window
lanes as rows, each a groove with its cards in a line

variants.reason: B keeps the cards as the only raised parts and spends the recess on the count, which is the board's state (P2 depth, P1 colour); A buries a raised card in a recessed well of almost the same grey so both lose their edge, and C turns cards into narrow tiles whose titles wrap and whose order is read along the line instead of down it.

root.why: The columns stand in one row inside the board and the row scrolls sideways when they do not fit, so a card arriving never changes the size of the unit.

column.why: A column keeps one fixed width and a seam on its inline start, so columns hold their places whatever cards they contain.

head.why: The title and the count window share one row on the column's inset line, so the printing reads like the label of a rack bay.

title.why: The column title is the emphasis size in the medium weight, one grotesk with hierarchy by size and weight only.

count.why: The count sits in a small recessed window with the well elevation and a ring hairline, the same display recess as every other window.

flag.why: The warning mark shows beside the figures when a column holds more cards than its limit, a shape cue that never uses colour.

body.why: The area under the head holds the list or the empty slot at a minimum height of three cards, so a column does not collapse when it empties.

list.why: The cards of a column stand in one stack with the same gap between each, in the order the person left them.

card.why: A task is the Card of this system at small padding, so it keeps the raised body, lit lip and radius that nest, and it takes the focus as one part.

cardHead.why: The card title and its keys stand in one row, with the keys at the inline end where the hand expects them.

cardTitle.why: The card title uses the body size in primary ink and wraps instead of cutting, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks.

detail.why: The line under the title is the caption size in secondary ink, so the title stays the first thing read.

tools.why: The grip and the Move key sit side by side with no gap and each is 44px square, so a thumb finds one without touching the other.

grip.why: The grip is the pointer handle of a card: it stops the page scrolling under a finger that drags, and it is hidden from assistive tech because the keys and the Move key do the same job.

empty.why: A column with no cards prints a recessed slot with one plain line of words, so an empty column reads as a place cards can go.

data-dragging=true.why: The carried card follows the pointer, is lifted by a pressed key's shadow and stays above its neighbours, so the move is told by position and shadow.

data-drop=before.why: A line drawn on the block-start edge of a card says the carried card will land before it, without moving any card.

data-drop=after.why: A line drawn on the block-end edge of the last card says the carried card will land at the end of the column.

data-over=true.why: An empty column under a carried card draws its slot with a heavier ring, so the target is told by a line weight.

data-over-limit=true.why: A column past its limit prints its figures in the medium weight with the warning mark beside them, which is readable without colour.

data-disabled=true.why: A card that cannot be moved loses its grip and fades to half, so it reads as fixed in its place.

focus-visible.why: A card that holds the keyboard focus shows the same dark focus ring as every part, so the person can see which card the arrow keys will move.

hover.why: The grip only darkens its ink a step on hover, because a real handle does not rise when a hand comes near.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the cards keep a real border in the text colour and the drop line uses the system highlight, so every edge stays a visible target.
